title: Dashboard Mount jog pad fires a 500 ms pulse guide instead of a slew - the arrows do nothing a user can see
what_happened: The Mount Control dashboard widget shows an N/S/E/W arrow pad that looks like a slew/jog pad. Each press calls mountCommandService.pulseGuide(direction), which the native log shows as 'Pulse guiding sim_mount_1 for 500ms in direction east' - about 4 arcseconds at guide rate. RA/Dec on the card stayed at 00:00:00 / +00d00'00" across three presses, no toast, no status change. Press-and-hold for 2 s produced exactly one 500 ms pulse, not a continuous slew.
expected: An arrow pad on a mount control card should slew (moveAxis / directional slew) at a user-selectable rate while held, as it does in NINA, SGP and the ASIAIR, and stop on release. If it really is a guide pulse it must be labelled as one and show the resulting offset.
repro: Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> enable Mount Control -> Done -> Unpark -> click the E arrow, then press-and-hold it for 2 s. Watch RA on the card and `tail /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log`.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log: '18:37:41 Pulse guiding sim_mount_1 for 500ms in direction east', '18:37:57 ... 500ms ...' (that one was a 2 s hold), '18:38:35 ... 500ms ...'. Card RA unchanged in /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-wizards-30.png and -31.png.
proposed_fix: Bind the pad to a hold-to-slew (start on pointer down, stop on pointer up/cancel) using the mount's directional slew, and add a slew-rate selector next to the existing tracking-rate selector.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly on the rebuilt bundle. Enabled the Mount Control tile, connected the sim mount, unparked; one click on the E chevron produced a single native log line '2026-08-03T20:48:05 INFO Pulse guiding sim_mount_1 for 500ms in direction east' and the card's RA stayed 00h 00m 00s. Press-and-hold via xdotool mousedown/2.5s/mouseup produced EXACTLY ONE further 500 ms pulse, not a continuous slew (counted 'Pulse guiding' lines appended to /tmp/ns-audit/v2-wizards/app.log). Location is exact: mount_control_card.dart:173-182 is the _MountDirectionalPad construction, :176 'onDirection: (direction) async {', :179 '.pulseGuide(direction);'. mount_command_service.dart:375 is 'Future<CommandActionResult> pulseGuide(String direction, {int durationMs = 500})' and the card never passes a duration, so every press is the 500 ms default.

title: Flat wizard's "Flat capture failed - no frames were saved" gives no reason and no next step
what_happened: Quick Capture ramped the exposure 0.17s -> 0.42 -> 1.0 -> 2.39 -> 5.75 -> 13.79 -> 30.0 s and the measured ADU crept only from ~1050 to 1361 against a target of 32768. After ~60 s it stopped with the red banner 'Flat capture failed - no frames were saved.' and the status chip 'Failed'. Nothing says what failed: not that the target ADU was unreachable, not that the 30 s exposure ceiling was hit, not that the ADU barely moved as exposure grew 170x (which is the actual diagnosis - the panel is not illuminating the sensor).
expected: Name the failure: 'Could not reach 32768 ADU - at the 30 s maximum the frame only reached 1361 ADU. Increase panel brightness or gain.' And when ADU does not scale with exposure, say so ('brightness did not change when exposure increased 170x - is the flat panel switched on?').
repro: Flat Wizard -> Quick Capture -> Frames 5 -> Start Capture -> pick a folder -> Continue. Wait ~60 s.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-146.png (red banner 'Flat capture failed - no frames were saved.', header 'EXPOSURE 30.00s ADU 1361 FRAME 0/5', chip 'Failed'); /tmp/ns-audit/r-wizards/app.log 14:50:34-14:51:34 exposure ramp.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/flat_wizard/ (action_buttons / status banner) and the flat capture service that raises the failure
proposed_fix: Carry a typed failure reason (targetUnreachable / exposureCeiling / adduNotResponding / saveFailed) through to the banner and render the measured-vs-target numbers.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim and root-caused. Sim camera + sim filter wheel connected, Imaging -> Camera -> Flat Wizard -> Quick Capture, filter R, target 50% (~32768 ADU), Start Capture. Exposure ramped 2.39s (ADU 1049) -> 13.79s (ADU 1198) -> 30.00s (ADU 1364), status chip 'Failed', red banner 'Flat capture failed - no frames were saved.' - within 3 ADU of the reported 1361. Grepped the ENTIRE a11y tree for 'max exposure', 'under target', 'panel brightness', 'converge': only hit was the chart title 'ADU Convergence'. ROOT CAUSE sharper than the finding: the reason IS computed and stored but has no reader. flat_wizard_service.dart:1136 returns errorMessage 'Max exposure reached but still under target' (siblings :1148, :1160), flat_wizard_provider.dart:1019-1023 does setWarningMessage('<filter>: <errorMessage>'), but NO widget under screens/flat_wizard/ ever reads state.warningMessage - the only rendered message is state.errorMessage (action_buttons.dart:17 and :32), which _setFinalStatus (flat_wizard_provider.dart:1310-1311) sets to the generic literal. 'where' is accurate; fix is a one-line surface.

title: Collaborative Sky still says "No collaborative mosaics on this hub yet" right after you publish one
what_happened: From the mosaic project screen I pressed 'Publish to hub'. The project screen immediately showed 'Hub mosaic fb402dd3-061d-4705-9b6b-ffbb1b441629 - Owner', 'Status: Published' and claimed all 6 panels. I then went to Plan Tonight -> Discover -> Collaborate on the same hub connection and the Collaborative mosaics section read 'No collaborative mosaics on this hub yet. Publish a mosaic project from its planner to split the panels across your club.' The hub disagrees: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/hub/hub.db 'select id,name from collaborative_mosaics' returns exactly that mosaic, with 6 panels all claimed. Pressing the refresh icon in the screen header made it appear.
expected: Publishing must invalidate the collaborative-mosaic list provider so the surface that exists to show shared mosaics does not tell the user there are none.
repro: Connect to a hub -> Analytics -> Projects -> Mosaic projects -> open a project -> Publish to hub -> Plan Tonight -> Discover -> Collaborate.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-197.png (project screen: 'Status: Published', hub mosaic id) then /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-199.png (Collaborate: 'No collaborative mosaics on this hub yet'); hub DB row above; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-201.png (the same list after pressing Refresh, now showing 'M31 Wide Field').
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/collaborative_sky/collaborative_sky_screen.dart (mosaic list provider) and the publish action on packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/mosaic/mosaic_project_screen.dart
proposed_fix: ref.invalidate the hub-mosaic list provider after a successful publish (and after join/claim), or make the list a stream.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by source; could not be driven end-to-end because no skotiq_hub is running on this machine (/tmp/ns-audit/hub/ does not exist, no hub process up) and standing one up was out of scope. The code is unambiguous. collaborative_sky_providers.dart:19 declares 'final collaborativeMosaicsProvider = FutureProvider<List<CollabMosaic>>((ref) { return ref.watch(collaborativeMosaicServiceProvider).listMosaics(); });' - NOT autoDispose, so its AsyncValue is cached for the container's life and survives leaving and re-entering the screen. Repo-wide there are exactly two non-test references: the watch at collaborative_sky_screen.dart:639 and one invalidate at collaborative_sky_screen.dart:81 inside _refresh(), which is only the manual header refresh icon - matching the finding's 'pressing the refresh icon made it appear'. The publish path never touches it: mosaic_project_controller.dart:507-526 publishToHub() does 'await collaborative.publishProject(_projectId); await load();' and load() only reloads that controller's own project. The list is guaranteed warm-and-empty before the publish because the Collaborative Sky screen is where the hub connection is made. 'where' is accurate.

title: The Smart Night dashboard prompt never appears even with its toggle on and every documented precondition met
what_happened: Settings -> Sequencer -> Smart Night Defaults -> 'Dashboard auto-prompt' ('Show the Smart Night prompt on the dashboard when your equipment is ready') is ON by default and I confirmed the toggle is blue/on. I then satisfied every gate the card checks (smart_night_prompt_card.dart:118-127): profile focal length 550 mm and aperture 100 mm saved (equipmentReady), observing location 40.0 / -105.0 and not 0,0, no sequence running, nothing dismissed on a fresh profile, and I waited more than four minutes - well past the 60 s readiness grace. The bottom-centre prompt never appeared, on the briefing dashboard or the cockpit dashboard.
expected: With the toggle on and equipment ready the prompt should slide in from the bottom centre. Either it shows, or the setting should not promise it.
repro: Fresh profile -> Settings -> Location: 40 / -105 -> Equipment -> Edit Profile -> focal length 550, aperture 100 -> connect the four simulators -> Dashboard -> wait 4 minutes.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-212.png (dashboard right after connecting), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-213.png (bottom strip 60 s later), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-214.png (four minutes in - no prompt anywhere); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rw-217.png and rw-218.png (the 'Dashboard auto-prompt' row and its toggle, on).
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/smart_night_prompt_card.dart:118-144 - the two remaining suppressors are the 60 s grace rebuild (_equipmentReadyGraceElapsed / _graceTimer) and 'if (draftAsync.isLoading || draftAsync.valueOrNull != null) return SizedBox.shrink()' on pendingSmartNightDraftProvider; a provider that never leaves loading would hide the card forever with no trace.
proposed_fix: Log and test the two suppressors: give pendingSmartNightDraftProvider a timeout and treat an unresolved lookup as 'no draft', and assert the grace timer schedules a rebuild. Caveat: the equipment on this profile was connected via Discovery rather than assigned to the profile ('0 devices'), which the card does not check but a related provider might.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced and root-caused. Fresh v2-wizards profile: Settings -> Location 40.0 / -105.0 (scratch DB app_settings observer_latitude=40.0, observer_longitude=-105.0), Edit Profile focal length 550 / aperture 100 (equipment_profiles row 1|My Equipment|550.0|100.0), sim camera + mount connected, no sequence running, nothing dismissed, smartNightAutoPromptEnabled defaults true (app_settings.dart:384). Sat on the dashboard >4.5 minutes; the a11y tree never contained 'Hardware ready' or 'Smart Night will choose'. ROOT CAUSE: smart_night_prompt_card.dart:21 declares 'final smartNightPromptNowProvider = Provider<DateTime>((ref) => DateTime.now());' - a non-autoDispose Riverpod Provider, so DateTime.now() is evaluated once and cached for the container's life. _equipmentReadyGraceElapsed (:297-326) then does '_equipmentReadySince ??= now' and 'final elapsed = now.difference(_equipmentReadySince!)', which is ALWAYS Duration.zero, so readyGraceElapsed is permanently false, canPlan (:118-122) is permanently false, and the card returns SizedBox.shrink() forever. The 60 s _graceTimer fires once, setState rebuilds, elapsed is still zero, and because _graceTimer is left non-null the '??=' never re-arms it. 'where' (smart_night_prompt_card.dart:118-144) is accurate - :118-127 is exactly the canPlan/baseShouldShow block and :139-144 the draftAsync guard.
